condition_zh: 葡萄糖-6-磷酸脱氢酶缺乏症（G6PD缺乏症/蚕豆病）

lab_tests: G6PD quantitative enzyme activity assay (gold standard)
clinical_features: Acute hemolytic anemia after trigger exposure
diagnosis.gold_standard: Quantitative G6PD enzyme activity assay — do NOT test during acute hemolysis (reticulocytes have higher G6PD activity → false normal)

treatment.indication: Acute hemolytic episode — first and most critical step
During acute hemolysis to prevent acute kidney injury from hemoglobinuria
Severe neonatal hyperbilirubinemia to prevent kernicterus

complications: Chronic non-spherocytic hemolytic anemia (rare, Class A variants)

clinical_examples.description: A 4-year-old boy from Guangdong presents with acute pallor, jaundice, and dark 'cola-colored' urine 24 hours after eating fava beans. Hb drops from baseline 120 to 58 g/L. Urine dipstick positive for blood but no RBCs on microscopy (hemoglobinuria).
clinical_examples.key_findings: Fava bean ingestion → acute hemolysis → hemoglobinuria + anemia → classic G6PD deficiency presentation (favism)
clinical_examples.outcome: G6PD activity <10% of normal. Diagnosis: G6PD deficiency (G6PD Canton variant c.1376G>T). Treated with IV fluids and packed RBC transfusion. Discharged with trigger avoidance education and G6PD alert card.
